keyAssumptions: ROSTER BASIS: CBRE's IN-PLACE PRO-FORMA for calendar year 2027 (page 9), which is what the $424,760 in-place NOI, the $181,979 recovery line and the $632,559 effective gross revenue tie to. Annual rents are the CY2027 contractual amounts, so where a suite has a 2027 step the PSF here is a blend — the site plan's "current" rate is recorded in each tenant's rentSchedule.

The OM's In-Place Pro-Forma prints lease dates as month-year only (e.g. "Apr-18" / "Mar-29") with no day. Commencements are recorded as the FIRST day and expirations as the LAST day of the printed month — a stated convention, not a figure read off the document. Re-key the exact days from the rent roll in diligence; WALT and the rollover schedule move by at most a few weeks.

Four-way tie-out against the OM's printed totals: (a) 66,700 SF occupied + 9,894 SF vacant = 76,594 SF GLA; (b) 66,700 / 76,594 = 87.1% occupancy; (c) base rents sum to $450,580 = the OM's Total Tenant Revenue Occupied; (d) $632,559 EGR - $207,799 OpEx = $424,760 NOI. Tenant recoveries sum to $181,981 vs the $181,979 printed (rounding).

OCCUPANCY CONFLICT INSIDE THE OM: pages 2 and 3 headline "89%" occupancy, but the page-4 site plan and the page-9 pro-forma both show 66,700 occupied / 76,594 total = 87.1%, and page 2's own narrative says "87% occupied." 87.1% is the arithmetic answer and is what is recorded here; the 89% is an error in the marketing pages.

FOOD DEPOT TERM: the rent roll shows the PRIMARY term expiring April 2028. The page-3 "April 2038" is the FINAL expiration including remaining renewal options, and page 2 describes "12 years of total remaining lease term." WALT here is computed off contractual primary-term expiries, so Food Depot contributes its April 2028 date — the center's option-inclusive term is materially longer. The OM does not print the number, length or rent of Food Depot's options; get them from the lease.
NO PRICE AND NO CAP RATE are quoted — unpriced marketing package. Value must be underwritten off the $424,760 in-place NOI.

TAXES ARE NOT REASSESSED. The $50,862 CY2027 real-estate tax line is the 2026 budget grown forward; the OM states expressly that reassessment is the investor's responsibility. Troup County, GA reassesses on sale activity, so model the step-up to the purchase price.

Expenses are CBRE's model of the 2026 budget with non-recoverable ownership-specific expenses replaced by a $0.05/SF assumption; tenant reimbursements toward amortized deferred capital projects are modeled BELOW the NOI line.
NO SALES ARE DISCLOSED FOR FOOD DEPOT — the anchor carrying 61% of GLA and 43% of revenue has no productivity data in the book. That is the single biggest information gap in the deal.
The OM does not print a year built, a renovation year, individual rent steps, renewal-option terms, or any co-tenancy, exclusive or kickout clause. All left null rather than estimated.

redFlags.description: The anchor's primary term expires in April 2028 — inside 18 months of the analysis start — and Food Depot is 61% of GLA, 34% of base rent and 43% of total revenue. The OM's cash flow simply assumes the option is exercised. If it is not, roughly half the center's revenue is at risk and there is no replacement grocer in a trade area already served by Publix, Kroger and Walmart Neighborhood Market within a mile.

NO SALES DATA FOR FOOD DEPOT. The OM discloses sales for four small shops but nothing for the anchor, so its ability to renew — at $3.25/SF or at anything else — cannot be tested. Do not underwrite the renewal without store-level sales.

13% vacancy across four separate shop suites (9,894 SF), and the whole value-add case depends on leasing all of it. CBRE models 100% absorption by 1/1/2028; the CY2027 in-place NOI of $424,760 is a $5.55/SF number that only becomes the $638,497 shown for CY2028 if that lease-up lands on schedule.

The trade area is the weakest of the Project Evergreen Georgia assets: 3-mile average household income of $75,444 and median of $54,635, with 1-mile average income of just $55,329. Renter-occupied households outnumber owner-occupied within a mile (1,592 vs 887). This argues for cap-rate cushion and conservative rent-growth assumptions, not aggressive mark-to-market.
A-1 Cutz Hair Salon carries a 14% occupancy cost on $152 PSF of sales (OM-stated) — the weakest tenant health disclosed at the center.
Concentration in small local operators: outside Food Depot and Buddy's Home Furnishings, the roster is entirely local/regional credit with no investment-grade tenancy and no disclosed guaranties.
Taxes are NOT reassessed in the pro-forma; the $50,862 modeled tax line is 12% of NOI and a Georgia sale typically triggers a reassessment to the transaction price.

upsideItems.item: Lease up 9,894 SF across four shop suites
upsideItems.detail: Lease-up of 9,894 SF (13% of GLA) across four shop suites — CBRE models full absorption by 1/1/2028 at $15.00-$20.00/SF, and it is the main driver of the 7.62% 5-year NOI CAGR the OM headlines.
Demonstrated shop rent growth: the two most recent renewals (Liquor Depot and Klassy Beauty) came in at an average 20% spread, which is real evidence rather than a modeled assumption.
Shop mark-to-market: average shop rent is $14.94/SF against CBRE's $15.00-$20.00 market range, with The Mattress Suite ($13.13) and Klassy Beauty ($12.46) furthest below.

upsideItems.item: EV-charging interest not in the projections
upsideItems.detail: Several EV-charging operators have expressed interest in the site — incremental income CBRE has NOT projected in the cash flow.

upsideItems.item: Food Depot's $3.25/SF is exceptionally sticky income
upsideItems.detail: Food Depot's $3.25/SF is far below any market rent, which makes it exceptionally sticky income; the tenant has been in place 18 years and extended for 10 years in 2018. Treat this as income durability, not capturable upside — the options run to April 2038, so the spread cannot be harvested inside a normal hold.
Trade-area growth: 3-mile population growing 1.29% annually since 2020 with new residential under construction (Crossvine Village 125 homes, Phase II 45 homes) and 288 apartments delivered in 2024.

upsideItems.item: Low basis, well below replacement cost
upsideItems.detail: Basis: the OM markets the asset as well below replacement cost, and the in-place NOI is only $5.55/SF on 76,594 SF.

deals.notes: LaGrange Marketplace is a 76,594 SF Food Depot-anchored neighborhood center at the SR-29 / Youngs Mill Road intersection (21,110 VPD) in LaGrange, Georgia, one mile from downtown and 2.5 miles from I-85, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. The center is 87.1% leased and generates $424,760 of CY2027 in-place NOI on $632,559 of effective gross revenue against $207,799 of operating expenses — a $5.55/SF NOI that reflects both the low rent basis and the 13% vacancy. Food Depot, an employee-owned regional grocer with 40+ Georgia stores, has operated here since 2008, extended for ten years in 2018, and occupies 61% of the GLA at just $3.25/SF, which is 34% of base rent and 43% of total revenue. That rent is far below market and therefore very sticky income, but it is locked by options running to April 2038 and cannot be marked to market inside a normal hold — and the OM discloses no store sales, so the anchor's health is untested even though its primary term expires in April 2028. Grocery competition in the trade area is fully defined and long-established, with Publix, Kroger and a Walmart Neighborhood Market all within one mile and each in place for 11+ years, which the broker frames as evidence Food Depot has carved out a durable value niche. The investment case is the 9,894 SF of vacancy across four shop suites plus a demonstrated 20% average rent spread on the two most recent renewals, together driving CBRE's 7.62% five-year NOI CAGR. The trade area is the weakest in this portfolio group — $75,444 3-mile average household income and $54,635 median — which argues for cap-rate cushion rather than aggressive rent growth, notwithstanding 1.3% annual population growth and several hundred new homes and apartments under construction nearby. The top risk is unambiguous: a single below-market grocer with no disclosed sales carries nearly half the revenue and reaches a term decision within eighteen months.
